 Live Score Thai Port vs Beijing Guoan: Goal Fest Marks Intense Asian Champions League Duel
 A seven-goal thriller unfolded in the first half of the AFC Champions League Elite match between Thai Port FC and Beijing Guoan.
 By: Damar Prasetya 
 | 
 Editor: Nayla Savitri 
 | 
 Contributor: Niken Pramudya 
 November 3, 2026, 21:36 WITA · 5 min read 
 Photo Caption: Illustration of the Thai Port FC vs Beijing Guoan match in the 2026/2027 AFC Champions League Elite, Tuesday (11/3/2026). Both teams engaged in an intense duel with seven goals scored in the first half. (Illustration/Aktualita.co) 
 PATHUM THANI, Aktualita.co -  The Thai Port FC vs Beijing Guoan match featured a seven-goal drama in just the first 45 minutes of the 2026/2027 AFC Champions League Elite continuation, Tuesday (11/3/2026) evening. 
 Playing at the True BG Stadium, Pathum Thani, Thailand, both teams engaged in a back-and-forth goal exchange from the opening minutes. Beijing Guoan even had to work hard to maintain their lead after the hosts managed to turn the situation around twice. 
 Advertisement 
 Beijing Guoan closed the first half with a 4-3 lead. Based on match updates up to the 53rd minute, that scoreline still held as both teams continued their battle in the second half. 
 This match drew attention as it brought together two teams with contrasting conditions in the East region standings. Thai Port arrived without a win in their previous three matches, while Beijing Guoan remained undefeated. 
 Flow of the Thai Port vs Beijing Guoan Match 
 Beijing Guoan applied pressure from the moment the first whistle blew. The visitors only needed five minutes to open the scoring through Chadrac Akolo. 
 The quick goal forced Thai Port to change their approach. Instead of continuing to defend, the hosts began to dare to launch counterattacks to chase the deficit. 
 The change paid off in the 17th minute. Jude Soonsup-Bell managed to equalize to 1-1 after capitalizing on a pass from Bordin Phala. 
 Just three minutes later, Soonsup-Bell added his name to the scoresheet again. This time, the Thai Port striker received a pass from Chaiyaphon Otton to put his team ahead 2-1. 
 However, that lead did not last long. 
 Beijing Guoan equalized again in the 23rd minute through Dawhan, who capitalized on an assist from Zhang Xizhe. The score changed to 2-2. 
 The match became even more interesting after Bordin Phala scored in the 29th minute. The goal put Thai Port back in the lead at 3-2, demonstrating the effectiveness of the hosts' attacks despite not dominating possession. 
 Beijing Guoan Rises, First Half Ends 3-4 
 Just as Thai Port seemed to find their rhythm, Beijing Guoan responded again. 
 Towards the end of the first half, an own goal by Noboru Shimura made the score 3-3. 
 Momentum then shifted to the visitors. 
 Dawhan scored his second goal of the match just before halftime. The goal ensured Beijing Guoan took a 4-3 lead after having trailed twice. 
 Seven goals in one half illustrated how open both teams' defenses were. 
 Beijing Guoan dominated possession, but Thai Port showed sharpness whenever they found space to launch quick attacks. 
 Entering the second half, the match remained tight. Up to the 53rd-minute update, Beijing Guoan led 4-3 with approximately 66 percent possession. 
 During that period, both teams had taken seven shots each. Thai Port recorded five shots on target, while Beijing Guoan had three. 
 The statistics show that greater possession did not automatically mean Beijing Guoan fully controlled the threats from the hosts. 
 Thai Port's Condition Before Facing Beijing Guoan 
 Before this match, Thai Port was in a difficult situation in the AFC Champions League Elite. 
 The Thai representatives suffered three consecutive defeats in the league phase. They lost 1-2 to Vissel Kobe, were thrashed 1-5 by Kashiwa Reysol, and then fell 0-3 to Johor Darul Ta'zim. 
 That string of negative results left Thai Port languishing in 15th place in the East region standings without a single point. 
 However, their performance in domestic competition showed a different picture. 
 Thai Port managed to beat Bangkok United 2-0 and Rayong FC 4-1 in two Thai League matches leading up to the meeting with Beijing Guoan. 
 This difference in performance posed a challenge for coach Božidar Bandović to build consistency in his players when facing opponents with higher quality of play. 
 Beijing Guoan Arrives with Seven Points 
 On the other hand, Beijing Guoan entered the match with a more convincing record. 
 The Chinese club collected seven points from three matches after recording two wins and one draw. 
 Beijing Guoan started the competition with a 3-1 win over Pohang Steelers. They then defeated Buriram United 1-0 before drawing 2-2 against Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors. 
 Those results placed Beijing Guoan in fifth place in the East region standings before the match against Thai Port. 
 Under the guidance of Nick Montgomery, Beijing Guoan showed consistent attacking ability and relatively stable team organization. 
 However, the match against Thai Port also showed that their defense could still be breached, especially when the opponent transitioned quickly into attack. 
 Thai Port vs Beijing Guoan Lineups 
 Thai Port fielded Michael Falkesgaard as goalkeeper, supported by Peerawat Akkratum, Erik Sviatchenko, Marcel Scalese, and Chaiyaphon Otton. 
 In the midfield were Seksan Ratree, Noboru Shimura, Worachit Kanitsribumphen, and Sittha Boonlha. Meanwhile, Jude Soonsup-Bell and Bordin Phala were the mainstays in building attacks. 
 Beijing Guoan relied on Hou Sen in goal, along with Wang Gang, Uros Spajic, Guilherme Ramos, and Bai Yang. 
 Jeremy Dudziak, Dawhan, Boubacar Konte, and Zhang Xizhe filled the midfield sector, while Beni Nkololo and Chadrac Akolo were threats to the hosts' defense. 
 Asnawi Mangkualam Not in Squad 
 For Indonesian football fans, the Thai Port match was also interesting because the Thai club is the team strengthened by Asnawi Mangkualam. 
 However, the Indonesian national team defender was not on the match roster against Beijing Guoan. 
 Asnawi previously suffered an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in January 2026, which required him to undergo surgery and a rehabilitation process. 
 In a club statement last January, Thai Port stated: 
 "Asnawi suffered an ACL injury in training and has successfully undergone surgery." 
 Asnawi's absence meant that attention in this match was focused more on the performance of the Thai Port attacking line, which managed to provide fierce resistance to the Chinese representatives. 
 Competition Towards the Round of 16 
 The match between Thai Port and Beijing Guoan is significant for the AFC Champions League Elite East region league phase competition. 
 The top eight teams out of the 16 East region participants are entitled to continue their journey to the round of 16. 
 For Beijing Guoan, a win would strengthen their position in the race for the knockout phase. 
 Meanwhile, for Thai Port, every point is very valuable after failing to get positive results in their opening three matches. 
 With seven goals scored since the first half, this duel became one of the most open matches in the fourth week's series. 
 Although Beijing Guoan is in a more favorable position, the sharpness of Jude Soonsup-Bell and Bordin Phala showed that Thai Port still has a chance to provide resistance until the final whistle. 
 Update note: The 3-4 score is the interim result confirmed up to the 53rd minute, not the final match result.
